top_level_objectives: Represent physical quantities as vectors with magnitude and direction.
Add and decompose vectors in two dimensions using graphical and trigonometric methods.
Relate vector components to projectile motion and explain the independence of horizontal and vertical motion.
Predict how launch speed and angle affect projectile trajectory, range, and maximum height.

scenes.brief_purpose: Establish the meaning of a vector as a quantity with both size and direction before connecting it to motion.
key_visuals: A 2D coordinate plane anchored in the AR space
Several arrows of different lengths and directions labeled as vectors
Simple magnitude and angle readouts attached to a selected vector
student_actions: Inspect and compare vectors by looking at their lengths and orientations
Select a vector and identify its magnitude and direction
Move or rotate a vector to see how changing length or angle changes the represented quantity

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how two vectors combine to produce a resultant using a geometric construction.
key_visuals: Two movable vectors on the same coordinate plane
A ghosted tip-to-tail placement guide
A resultant vector drawn from the first tail to the final tip
student_actions: Drag one vector to the tip of another to build a tip-to-tail sum
Predict the direction and size of the resultant before revealing it
Compare cases where vectors reinforce or partially cancel each other

scenes.scene_name: Decomposing a Vector into x and y Components
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect a single angled vector to perpendicular horizontal and vertical components.
key_visuals: One vector at an angle above the x-axis
Dashed projections to the x- and y-axes forming a right triangle
Component arrows labeled x-component and y-component with values
student_actions: Adjust the angle and magnitude of the vector and observe how its components change
Use the right-triangle picture to relate the vector to its horizontal and vertical parts
Identify which component grows or shrinks as the angle changes

scenes.scene_name: From Components to Magnitude and Direction
scenes.brief_purpose: Reinforce the mathematical relationship between components, vector magnitude, and direction.
key_visuals: A right triangle built from the component vectors
Magnitude shown as the hypotenuse and direction shown as an angle from the x-axis
Simple formula overlays linking components to trigonometric relationships
student_actions: Estimate a vector’s magnitude and direction from displayed components
Check predictions against the reconstructed full vector
Test multiple examples to see how the same methods work for different component values

scenes.scene_name: Initial Velocity of a Projectile as a Vector
scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector decomposition to the launch of a projectile.
key_visuals: A launcher on a flat ground plane with an initial velocity arrow at an adjustable angle
Horizontal and vertical velocity components drawn from the launch point
A faint predicted trajectory arc extending from the launcher
student_actions: Set a launch speed and angle
Decompose the initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components
Predict whether changing angle or speed will alter the components more strongly in x or y

scenes.scene_name: Independence of Horizontal and Vertical Motion
scenes.brief_purpose: Show that projectile motion can be understood as constant horizontal motion combined with vertically accelerated motion.
key_visuals: A projectile moving along a parabolic path
Separate side-by-side or overlaid views of horizontal motion and vertical motion
Velocity arrows at several points showing constant horizontal component and changing vertical component
A gravity indicator pointing downward
student_actions: Play the launch and pause at different points to inspect velocity components
Observe that equal time intervals give constant horizontal spacing but changing vertical motion
Explain how gravity changes only the vertical component while leaving the horizontal component unchanged

scenes.scene_name: Exploring How Launch Conditions Shape the Trajectory
scenes.brief_purpose: Synthesize the vector ideas by linking launch angle and speed to range, peak height, and overall path.
key_visuals: Multiple projectile trajectories overlaid for different launch settings
Markers indicating maximum height and landing point for each trial
Live readouts for launch angle, speed, range, and peak height
student_actions: Run several launches while varying angle and speed one at a time
Compare trajectories to identify how range and maximum height respond to each change
Infer the role of the initial velocity components in producing the observed parabolic paths
